try to tell us how each group will suffer if they take only 6 per cent. One by one, we are told that the government's plans will not work.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Why do you not move back to your riding?

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
They say that the government's plans will not work and that inflation will triumph. They are telling us that, one by one, individual groups will fall behind or suffer a crushing extra load, or be left at the side of the road to wither and die. One by one, they are dividing people in our economy. One by one, they are hoping to conquer. They are hoping to conquer because they know that without co-operation the government will fail. They know that if they continue that kind of division, then inflation will indeed continue and will run wild.
However, not everyone in our economy has gone along with them. They have offered their divide and conquer rule on behalf of some senior citizens and some former civil servants. Yet they only have to open the Ottawa Citizen to note the reaction of some of those very people. Let me quote from the Ottawa Citizen of June 30. This is not what I say, this is what the people themselves say. On June 30 page 31 of the Ottawa Citizen, under the title "We are citizens ... we'll cut back", Mr. George Wagdin, past president of the Senior Citizens' Council of Ottawa, stated:
-I think we all have to share the burden that MacEachen faces.
The article goes on to state:
Bert Hanmer, vice-chairman of the Ottawa-Carleton Council on Aging, is pleased those at the lowest end of the income scale eligible for guaranteed income supplements won't be affected . ..
He feels everyone who can afford to cut back, including seniors, should.
"We're citizens as well as seniors."
Dorothy Milligan, of the Senior Citizens Council and a retired public servant, said the changes may mean she has to give up a few luxuries, but they won't mean hardship.
Milligan said she would have been very concerned about the budget changes had the government not protected the lowest income seniors. But since they've been looked after, "1 think the rest of us ought to tighten our belts a little bit and get this thing licked."
We have all or nothing, we have divide and conquer, but this government will not take either course.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: We have a big hoax and a big con job over there.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: This government is taking a middle of the road course which was best described by the advice given to us in The Financial Post-

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: it is Karl Marx's socialism over there.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: -the very pinnacle of business advice. Let me give some advice from The Financial Post to my hon. friends across the way.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Oh, oh!

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext:
The Financial Post of July 3, 1982, states:
The opposition, sensing weakness, may go for the jugular and forget that they, too, have a constructive role to play at times of very delicate balance.
The extreme and the implacable, egged on by the excitable in the media and unable to see merit in a middle way, may blindly help precipitate an even deeper crisis for Canada.
There are great risks facing us. And because they are so large, the minister's attempt to make a new start-and to make us all face the realities of the worldwide recession-should be treated seriously and dissected with restraint...
In these circumstances, there should be a pause for cool consideration of what is a very wide ranging budget, a thoughtful moment to examine where best interests do in fact lie over the longer term, and exactly how best Canadians can work their way out of the present crunch.
That is important advice for all of us from the July 3 edition of The Financial Post.
We are not asking Canadians to carry a huge burden. We are asking Canadians to contribute a small amount each. Why? It is so that they can share some of that with people in great need, people who need jobs, people who need houses, people whose businesses need some help. Those are the people whom we are anxious to help. If senior citizens and if ordinary people can go along with it, then surely it is not too much to ask that some of our colleagues here in the House go along with it.
I close on this advice, that all of us here should begin, perhaps, to make fewer of the gestures and comments which have been so eloquently directed to me tonight and, instead, we should lift our eyes and see that this country-

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: To the hills.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Oh, oh!

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: -has need of unity and has need of some constructive advice.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Hear, hear!

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Finance
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Surely, if we can get the kind of enthusiasm and see the kind of assistance that ordinary retired citizens can give us, it is not too much to ask that all of us in this House, together, seriously consider the problems facing our economy and contribute as much as each of us can to their solution.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Hear, hear!

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Madam Speaker, I do not want to appear as if I do not understand the rules, but I wonder if you might explain to me exactly what is happening at the moment?

speakerposition: Speaker of the House of Commons
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: There was a misunderstanding, apparently, about whether the Speaker would wait beyond the 15-minute bell. There was a misunderstanding as to whether or not it was a 15-minute bell. There was some confusion about the information that was given at the time. However, I am told that the members are now coming to the chamber to vote and I will wait a few minutes more.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Oh, oh!

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Madam Speaker, as an official of the chair I might be breaking with long-standing tradition when I ask to be recognized, but I have to dissociate myself from what is happening right now. We have long-standing practices here, and rules of procedure that we all obey. This is a 15-minute bell, and I cannot continue in my responsibilities if members are not going to obey the rules and procedures. Therefore, I am telling my Prime Minister (Mr. Trudeau) and the members of my caucus that I cannot serve as an officer of the chair because those members not present do not comport themselves according to the rules and procedures. They are not acting as true representatives of this country. I am very sorry I have to announce that now, but if the vote is not taken now, I am sorry, I cannot put up with that.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Hear, hear!

speakerposition: Speaker of the House of Commons
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I can assure the hon. member that the vote will be taken momentarily.

speechtext:
Now.

speakerposition: Speaker of the House of Commons
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: I would ask the hon. member to reconsider his decision. Perhaps he is not aware of what had transpired previously. I was informed just as I occupied the chair, that apparently there was some confusion concerning information given about the length of time the bells could ring. That is why some members are meeting and did not come down at the appropriate time. I will be taking the vote momentarily. I would very much regret the hon. member not wanting to serve again in the capacity in which the Chair has given him full confidence. I would ask him to reconsider his decision in light of what happened just before 1 occupied the chair.

subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Madam Speaker, if I may, I would like to speak to the matter raised by the hon. member for Glengarry-Prescott-Russell (Mr. Ethier). I hope that, before he gives any finality to what he has indicated to the House today, he would consult very carefully with his seatmate, the Deputy Speaker, with the officers of the Table, with Madam Speaker and with one member in particular from my party, the hon. member for York-Peel (Mr. Stevens). By doing that he will understand exactly what occurred tonight. I do not want to make any point. Others will argue about it perhaps. But I wanted to say that to my hon. friend who, in the sense of my riding, is almost a neighbour. I hope the hon. member will reconsider the matter.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
subsubtopic: FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE MINISTER OF FINANCE
speechtext: Madam Speaker, I appreciate the kind words of the hon. member for Nepean-Carleton (Mr. Baker). I meant what I said before; I do not speak with a forked tongue, and I stand by what I said. When an order of this House is given for a 15-minute bell and members are called to vote, if that order is not going to be obeyed, I cannot be an officer of the chair. I stand by what I said a while ago. I will not be an officer of the chair any further if members do not live by the rules and procedures that were given by them to the Chair. Therefore, I stand by what I said a while ago. Please accept my resignation, Madam Speaker.
